[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Route Groups and Private Folders in Next.js"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"As your Next.js application grows, organizing your codebase efficiently becomes crucial. The App Router introduces powerful folder conventions like Route Groups and Private Folders to help you structure your project without affecting the final URL hierarchy."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"What are Route Groups?"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Route Groups allow you to organize your files into logical groupings without impacting the URL path. By wrapping a folder name in parentheses, such as (folderName), you instruct Next.js to omit that folder from the generated routes."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Organize routes by feature, department, or user roles instead of URL paths."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enable multiple root layouts in the same application."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cleanly separate marketing pages from dashboard or application pages."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Route Groups Example Structure"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Consider the following file structure where we separate marketing pages from shop pages:"},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"app/
  (marketing)/
    about/
      page.js
    contact/
      page.js
    layout.js
  (shop)/
    account/
      page.js
    cart/
      page.js
    layout.js"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Despite being inside folders named (marketing) and (shop), the resulting URLs remain /about, /contact, /account, and /cart."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"What are Private Folders?"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Private Folders allow you to securely store implementation details, components, or helper functions directly inside the app directory by prefixing the folder name with an underscore, like _folderName."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Excludes the folder and all its subdirectories from routing."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Prevents accidental route generation for utility files or UI components."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Simplifies code separation between pages and components."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Private Folders Example Structure"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"app/
  _components/
    Button.js
    Navbar.js
  dashboard/
    page.js"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this setup, even though _components resides inside the app directory, requesting the URL /_components will result in a 404 error because the underscore marks it as private."},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"By combining Route Groups and Private Folders, you gain complete control over your Next.js application architecture. Use Route Groups to manage layouts and logical feature boundaries, and use Private Folders to keep utility components safely out of the routing system."}]
